== Biography ==
William is currently recorded as born about 1735, attached as a son of [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] and [[Rutherford-4861|Margaret Rutherford]], and as having died about 1829 in the United States. The cited basis is a user-contributed FamilySearch tree; no inspected original record yet proves those events or relationships.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1025]] is assessed at 46% (possible). William’s c 1735 birth fits a c 1700 father, and the contributed family account identifies James Glasgow with Margaret Rutherford. This gives a chronologically workable candidate couple.

Possible family-tree inference; William’s vital facts and the parental placement lack a held contemporary proof.

Next useful test: Locate William’s marriage or James’s probate with an explicit kin relationship.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-2426 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-2426]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Killycurragh generations, 20 October 2026 ===

The freshly read published transcription of PRONI T1959/3 distinguishes an older William of Killycurragh, the writer’s paternal great-grandfather, from his son William, the writer’s paternal grandfather and husband of Miss Cunningham. The younger William is the Cunningham husband, whose sons included James and Samuel. His son John married Margaret Glasgow after ordination at Coleraine and died at his father’s house in Orritor in July 1801. The surviving child, the anonymous writer, was born five months later; Margaret died in 1817. The separate church compilation identifies John Glasgow from Orritor, ordained at New Row, Coleraine, on 8 March 1796 and dead on 13 July 1801. The shared ministry, origin, name and death month strongly identify the husband. The writer separately describes Margaret’s father William as a son of James Glasgow and Margaret Rutherford; the two parental lines must not be collapsed into one grandfather.

Select [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]] as the possible father of the letter-defined Cunningham husband at 36%. The letter supplies an older Killycurragh William, son of the Tullycoll/Tullyall William and brother of James (husband of Margaret Rutherford) and John (husband of Anne Mason). The 1705 Kirknewton child William has a named father William and a generation compatible with being grandfather of the minister ordained in 1796. The 1702 John baptism supplies a compatible second named son in that Scottish father cluster; the existing James-1025 family supplies the Irish James comparison. This is a positive but non-exclusive family-cluster hypothesis. The Scottish child’s adult identity and migration remain unproved. The 36% includes that identity uncertainty; it is not a confident Scottish–Irish bridge.

Select the letter-defined William of Killycurragh as Rev. John Glasgow’s father at 94% (strongly supported). The writer explicitly gives the writer’s father John, the writer’s paternal grandfather William and his Cunningham marriage. John’s Coleraine ordination, Orritor origin and July 1801 death match the separate New Row minister entry. This concerns the minister’s record-defined identity; it does not identify his grandfather with a Scottish baptism or upgrade his brothers’ later-profile matches.

Select [[Glasgow-2426|William Glasgow]] as Margaret Glasgow’s probable father at 84%. That profile represents William, son of [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] and Margaret Rutherford, which matches the letter’s maternal-grandfather family position. The letter explicitly names the eldest daughter Margaret as the minister’s wife and the writer’s mother. The profile’s circa-1735 birth and circa-1829 United States death are inherited claims, not exclusionary records and not corrected here. The letter calls William an eldest son; the circa-1735 estimate conflicts with the earlier estimated births of his attached brothers. Those unverified estimates require checking and are preserved here. This is the maternal grandfather, distinct from the Cunningham husband. Original records and an independent adult-life bridge remain to be found.

These are exact subjective assessments of complete relationship-and-identity propositions, not measured probabilities. The family letter is undated and unsigned and is read through Albert Rutherford’s published transcription of a photocopy, not an inspected PRONI original. The minister list is a derivative compilation whose independence from the family tradition is unproved. The Scottish adult identities remain possible: neither the letter nor the 1705 baptism supplies a migration, occupation, property or witness bridge between Kirknewton and Tyrone. The letter’s three-son family and second-cousin statement are internally consistent clues from one source, not independent corroborations. Existing people, vital fields and mothers are preserved. Miss Cunningham and Anne Rutherford are reported maternal names, not transferred to existing maternal profiles. The letter’s first-settler story is family tradition, not proof of the first Glasgow in Tyrone or of the surname’s origin.<ref name="KillycurraghGenerations20261020">PRONI T1959/3, [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ published transcription], read 20 October 2026; original uninspected. [https://cotyrone.com/churchrecord/ministers-pres.html Minister compilation], John Glasgow, New Row; derivative entry, not an original register.</ref>

=== Moneymore place conflict ===

The structured birthplace “Moneymore, Galway, Connacht” combines a real place-name with a county that does not fit the Moneymore used in this family reconstruction. Moneymore in Artrea civil parish is in County Londonderry, not County Galway.<ref>[https://www.townlands.ie/londonderry/loughinsholin/artrea/moneymore/moneymore/ Townlands.ie, “Moneymore Townland, Co. Londonderry”], placing Moneymore in Artrea civil parish, barony of Loughinsholin, County Londonderry.</ref> This geographic correction does '''not''' prove that William was born in the Londonderry townland: several Irish places share the name, and no record inspected for William identifies one of them.

PRONI's official church-register guide lists First Moneymore Presbyterian baptisms only from 1827, Second Moneymore from 1845, and Ardtrea/Desertlin Roman Catholic baptisms from 1832.<ref>[https://www.proni.gov.uk/publications/proni-guide-church-records Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Guide to Church Records''], First Moneymore Presbyterian MIC1P/339; Second Moneymore Presbyterian MIC1P/340; Ardtrea/Desertlin MIC1D/35 and T3050; guide consulted 30 August 2026.</ref> None of those surviving series can record a birth about 1735. This explains the register gap but does not prove William's identity, birthplace or parents; deeds, estate papers, probate and other contemporary records remain the appropriate next search.

The current parents, sibling group, birth and death locations and estimated years are retained until evidence supplies replacements. They should be treated as unproved tree claims, as noted in [[Space:Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland|Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland]], rather than silently cleared or converted into a different family.

=== Possible William Glascoe, Maryland notice ===
A Lancaster Goal notice dated 13 October says John M’Connel, about 35, imprisoned as a suspected runaway servant, claims to belong to William Glascoe in Maryland, about forty miles from Baltimore.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39392109/ Pennsylvania Gazette, 1775-10-25, p.1].</ref>

The Maryland location is John M’Connel’s attributed claim, not independently proved residence. The notice gives no relatives for William or evidence that he was the 1760 London defendant.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2426]]. William’s estimated 1735 birth and later American context are chronologically compatible, but no record places him at the stated Maryland location.

=== Possible William Glasgow, Philadelphia and Charles-Town postal lists, 1759–1771 ===
William Glasgow, Cecil County, is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39399295/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1759-08-09, p.1].</ref>

William Glasgow is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office in February 1763.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39390517/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1763-02-24, p.1].</ref>

William Glasgow is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office in October 1765.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39405824/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1765-10-10, p.4].</ref>

William Glasgow is separately listed in the Charles-Town, Maryland, post-office letters notice headed 1 October 1771, beside an entry for John Glasgow of West Nottingham.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41041559/ Maryland Gazette, 1771-10-24, p.3].</ref>

Cecil County explicitly qualifies the 1759 entry only. In 1763 "Pennsylvania" follows James Gillispie; in 1765 "Forks of Delaware" qualifies William Greenlee, not William Glasgow. The entries may concern different men, and co-listing with John in 1771 does not prove a family relationship.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2426]]. Estimated 1735 birth and later United States context are unproved family account; no postal identification. The Moneymore County Galway field is disputed.
